actions.action: Add a “Move to position” command to every item.
actions.mechanism: An explicit destination avoids dragging or repeated movement through 40 items.
actions.implementation: Provide a keyboard-focusable button opening a labeled dialog with the current position and an integer field accepting 1–40. Enter applies the move; Escape cancels. Define the number as the item’s final position.
actions.check: Using only the keyboard, move item 37 to position 4. Verify its final position; reject 0, 41, and fractional values without changing the order.
actions.risk: Users may confuse insertion positions with final positions; label the field “Final position.”

actions.action: Offer a keyboard move mode for incremental ordering.
actions.mechanism: Users reposition the focused item while retaining its context.
actions.implementation: Activate move mode through a labeled button. Arrow Up/Down shifts the item one position; Home/End moves it to the first/last position. Enter commits one history entry; Escape restores the starting order. Handle these keys only inside move mode.
actions.check: Move an item several positions and cancel; verify exact restoration. Repeat and commit, then undo the entire move in one operation.
actions.risk: Unscoped key handlers can interfere with scrolling and assistive technology.

actions.action: Keep reversible order history for the page’s lifetime.
actions.mechanism: Retained order snapshots support undo without reconstructing inverse moves.
actions.implementation: Before each committed move, retain the previous ID sequence. Provide keyboard-accessible Undo, Redo, and history restoration controls. Preserve earlier snapshots after branching edits. Store history in tab-scoped sessionStorage to survive reloads; if persistence fails, reject the pending move with an accessible error.
actions.check: Make three moves, undo twice, make another move, then restore each earlier order. Reload the same tab and verify restoration still works.
actions.risk: Storage limits or blocked storage can prevent moves; never silently discard required history.

actions.action: Preserve focus and announce ordering changes.
actions.mechanism: Stable focus and concise feedback make movement and reversal understandable without visual tracking.
actions.implementation: After moving or undoing, focus the affected item’s move button. Use a polite live region to announce its title, final position, and list size. Expose position text on each item and give repeated move buttons item-specific accessible names.
actions.check: With keyboard and screen reader, move and undo an item. Verify focus remains on that item, its reported position matches the DOM, and each committed change produces one announcement.
actions.risk: Re-rendering or excessive announcements can lose focus or overwhelm users.

actions.action: Make ordering an atomic change to an ID sequence.
actions.mechanism: Separating item identity from position protects IDs and keeps visual, reading, and keyboard order aligned.
actions.implementation: Store item records by immutable ID and order separately as an ID array. Implement moves as remove-and-insert operations on a copy, validate the unchanged ID set, then commit order and history together. Render DOM order from this array using ID-based keys, not CSS ordering.
actions.check: Test all 1,600 source/destination pairs: length remains 40, every original ID appears exactly once, the destination is correct, and undo restores the exact prior sequence.
actions.risk: Index-based keys or partial updates can associate controls with the wrong item.
